Either way, dropping focus from a control that no longer shows should match the removal path's reading (the root element, the tree naming the window).

A focused control hidden by `hidden`, `style="display:none"` or CSS alone keeps focus and takes keys, and a select's choice still moves past its dropped anonymous block. The limit was owned by residual `res-6k56erh6`, by `escher-0.4.0-incubator/deferred-from-0.3.0.md` and by a CARRY on «A11y re-read». This is the origin of item 1. Widening the fixup to `display:none`/`hidden` changes a founder-chosen rule for every document, so it needs his ratification, and the no-blur choice must be re-decided for the new trigger.

Four engine debts left by 0.1.0-0.3.0, each researched with every option's cost and put to the founder as a fork in one file, then either fixed and proven headless on the stand (or as a fixture in both layout modes) or kept as a residual by his word.
Item 1: a focus fixup for a focused control that no longer renders (hidden attribute, display:none, CSS alone), which today keeps focus and takes keys because the fixup reads inertness alone — or keep the limit.
Item 2: a task polled during a Dioxus buffered render acting on the render's own new nodes (set_focus on a node created in that render), by a deferred or replayed act — or keep the limit.
Item 3: seeding a page script's Math.random from a document-level seed — or keep the limit; item 4: pruning the growing error-boundary registry by a reachable signal, waiting on a dioxus-core release, or keeping it.
A fix to items 1-3 is an engine change for every document, remote pages included, and crosses no new carrier, verb, argument, field, cause, log field or span unless the founder rules it.

body: The focus fixup that reads inertness alone: item 1 may widen it so a focused control that stops rendering (hidden attribute, display: none, CSS alone) gives up focus, possibly only after the next layout — a changed behaviour if the founder chooses the fix.

Removing or losing the focused node drops focus with blur steps: a focus given up by the new fixup must run the same blur and focus-event steps, and the keys it no longer takes must not reach the hidden control.

What is focusable and how Tab and Shift+Tab walk focus: a control no longer rendered must not be left focused nor be a stop the fix reintroduces; focusability recomputed on attribute writes stays the trigger set unless the fork rules otherwise.

Hidden content kept out of the accessibility tree (hidden, display: none, visibility: hidden, aria-hidden) and the inert subtree excluded: the focus fixup's notion of a no-longer-rendered control must agree with what the tree already drops, so the tree's focus never points at a node the tree omits.
The accessibility tree's focus value and its refresh on change: a focus change made by the fixup or by a deferred set_focus must mark the changed set so the tree and snapshot report the new focus.

The Dioxus render into a mutation buffer: item 2 may let a task polled during a render act on nodes that render created (a deferred or replayed act), changing what MountedData set_focus does on such a node, whose result set_focus_to now reports as false.
Hidden and inert nodes in hit-testing and the accessibility tree: an inert element takes no hit; the fix must not change hit or tree readings of hidden or inert nodes beyond the focus it gives up.

The page script runtime's randomness (item 3): seeding Boa's Math.random from a document-level seed reaches the script runtime's crossing and the seeded source's rule that it reads no environment variable, file or carrier — a fix must stay inside both.

The error-boundary registry and its root error mark (item 4): pruning dropped boundaries by a weak handle or generation, or naming the wait on a dioxus-core release, must leave boundary marks reported as they are for live boundaries.
No new carrier, verb, argument, field, cause, log field or span: the driver schema, snapshot fields, actions answer and log lines stay as they are unless the founder rules otherwise.

Proof of each fix headless on the stand or as a fixture in both layout modes: a new focus check beside the inert-subtree checks, and the spawned-acts probe pins for item 2 re-read against the changed render.

A focus clear for a control that no longer renders (item 1) is a focus change, so it must write the changed set at a sanctioned site. Adding a new write site amends that closed list, as the later select-list chunks did.

These are the key paths a hidden-but-focused control still takes (item 1), and the rows `decision/keyboard-activation-enter`/`-space` and `decision/click-focuses-button`. A module that glob-imports `dioxus::prelude::*` names `::keyboard_types`. Trap for item 2's probe and bridge tests in dioxus-native-dom (`decision/keyboard-types-named-by-absolute-path`).

It also stated the focus-fixup limit with a residual owner. This is the earlier engine-debts chunk this one follows: each fork was answered by the delegate PROVISIONAL and discharged later by the founder's batch (`amd-yiemoprt`). Item 1's fixup must reuse these one readings (`decision/disabled-one-reading`, `decision/inert-honoured`).

It is ratified as an API addition, flagged upstreamable. This is the nearest precedent for item 3's document-level seed: a config field whose default keeps behaviour, threaded to sub-documents (`decision/document-clock`, `contract/document-config/clock`). It also set the rule "No `Instant::now()` outside `clock.rs`" (`decision/no-wall-time-outside-clock`).

It was ratified per fork by the founder and its merge surface rides the upstream-sync CARRY. This is the precedent for how an engine change for every document is recorded (`decision/select-keyboard-model`).

body: A focus fixup for a control that is focused and then stops rendering (hidden attribute, display:none, CSS): whether focus is given up, when (after the next layout), and how it sits beside the inert focus clear and the inert subtree rule.

Indirect, through the focus clear the fixup extends: the existing inert focus clear fires no blur, and programmatic focus changes fire focus events; a new clear must take one of those rules deliberately and keep the inert clear as it is.
Indirect, through the accessibility adapter: accessibility focus names only a built node and the tree is refreshed on change, so a control that loses its box must not stay the adapter's focus.

A task polled during a Dioxus render made to see that render's own nodes (a deferred or replayed act), under the rule that Dioxus renders into a buffer before borrowing the document and that try_doc answers none while the document is borrowed.

Mounted-element operations on a missing node: setting focus on a node not yet in the document answers false and acts on nothing; a deferred act must keep the missing-node and removed-element answers and never panic on a stale node id.

Seeding a page script's Math.random from a document-level seed: the seeded source takes its seed from in-process code only and reads no environment variable, file or carrier, so the seed reaching the script runtime must come the same way.

Indirect, through the script runtime's crossing: JavaScript stays opt-in in the browser, the default script fetcher takes local, file and data URLs only, and script errors are recorded, not propagated; a seeding hook changes none of these.

The error-boundary registry and the root boundary error mark: pruning a dropped boundary by a reachable signal (a weak handle, a generation) must keep the root-boundary Err crossing as it is; a wait on a dioxus-core release is named as such.

A fix crosses no new carrier, verb, argument, field, cause, log field or span unless the founder rules it: the boundary widening rule, the closed driver verb schema, the closed refusal cause set and the engine target field allowlist hold.

A fix to debts 1 to 3 is an engine change for every document, remote pages included, and is its own ratification; untrusted page markup and scripts reach the new focus fixup, deferred act and seeded Math.random, so each stays finite and panic-free on hostile input.
Each fixed debt is proven headless on the stand or as a fixture in both layout modes; each kept debt stays a named residual with the founder's reason.
